title: Roadstorm versioned AI-observation fixture (schema version 1)
description: Fixture contract for the shared AIObservation record contract in observation_record.schema.json, defined at M0.9 from docs/OPPONENT_AI.md ('Architecture', 'Shared schema version 1', 'Training approach', 'Implementation and acceptance') and docs/BENCHMARKS.md ('AI metrics'). A fixture fixes one scenario (participant, difficulty, style, tick, per-car top speed, per-section usable half-width, observation-builder revision) and carries one or more observation records, plus the behavioral expectations the fixtures/observation validator checks semantically (context agreement, difficulty/style one-hot encoding, the declared per-feature kinds and ranges, neighbor presence masks, ordering and the 70 m ahead / 35 m behind window, traffic-age arithmetic and the difficulty age, reset history masking including the substituted-defaults list, normalization consistency including canonical raw_inputs keys, fallback defaults, null/unknowns pairing including an omitted optional field, the optional diagnostic neighbor_ids list, and the acceptance-metric status and shape rules) and the documented initial acceptance metrics. Like handling_fixture.schema.json and intent_fixture.schema.json, this is a text contract: numeric feature values are authored illustrative normalizations, never measurements. A value that is not yet determined is JSON null and MUST be listed in 'unknowns'; the validator enforces that pairing for the null-meaning-undetermined fields. Companion vocabulary lives in ../common.schema.json. This fixture defines no model, weights, export or training interface; the learned-style input exists so the shared contract can be exercised, not because a trained model exists.

schema_version.description: Contract revision identifier. A fixture whose schema_version differs is rejected, not silently migrated.

fixture_family.description: Which observation behavior the fixture exercises. 'regression' is reserved for fixtures added later for meaningful new concerns.

revision.description: Fixture content revision. Any semantic change to context, records, expectations or metrics bumps this and recomputes content_hash.

status.description: provisional = authored initial contract, not yet executed against an implementation; frozen = accepted after review; example = contract illustration that deliberately instantiates an unratified producer (e.g. a learned-style input) without claiming it exists. 'measured' is not valid here: fixtures carry targets and requirements, never measured outcomes.

tick_rate_hz.description: Fixed simulation tick rate (TECHNICAL_DESIGN 'Fixed tick and movement ownership').

participant_id.description: Participant every record in this fixture belongs to; records must agree with it.

top_speed_m_s.description: Per-car top speed used to normalize feature 0 (speed / top-speed). Authored illustrative value; exact per-car top speeds are handling parameters fixed at M1.

usable_half_width_m.description: Per-section usable road half-width used to normalize feature 4 (lane offset / usable half-width). Authored illustrative value; 0 is permitted only for the zero-usable-width safe-fallback case, which the validator requires to set fallback.active. WHICH half-width this names is unratified and is a blocking unknown recorded in every fixture's unknowns: OPPONENT_AI.md says 'usable half-width' without defining it, while its action-0 decode derives the narrower legal corridor (road_width - car_width)/2 - 0.5 m, and history features 51-52 are 'divided by their then-usable half-width' under the same undetermined convention. The shipped fixtures author road_width/2 (10 m -> 5.0, 12 m -> 6.0) as an illustrative value only; the convention must be ratified before demonstrations are collected, and this slice does not decide it.

observation_builder_revision.description: Revision of the ObservationBuilder code/configuration that produced these records, recorded like handling_fixture.schema.json's controller_revision. A placeholder string is acceptable only while the real revision is unratified and listed in the fixture unknowns.

traffic_age_is_difficulty_default.description: true when every record's traffic_age_ticks must equal the difficulty default (18/12/7). false lets a fixture exercise a non-default age, which then must be explained in the description; the validator cannot machine-check the prose, so the explanation stays a human responsibility.

records.description: Observation records. Each carries the 64-element normalized feature vector in fixed order and the timestamps/masks the semantic checks verify.

expectations.description: Behavioral expectations the validator checks. Each names a semantic check the validator implements and the record it applies to; a check id the validator does not implement is a fixture error, so expectations cannot drift from the executable checks.

metrics.description: Documented initial targets from OPPONENT_AI.md 'Implementation and acceptance'. A metric with status 'measured' is invalid in a fixture file and is rejected by the validator; measured values belong to evaluation records.

unknowns.description: Every null in a record field whose null means 'not yet determined' (occupancy_encounter_gap_m) must have a matching entry here, keyed by the dotted path including the record index, e.g. records.0.occupancy_encounter_gap_m. Entries may also record unratified decisions that have no null field.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 over canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8) of this file with the content_hash member removed. Recomputed by the validator on every check.

check.description: Semantic check implemented by fixtures/observation/validate_observation_contract.py. neighbor_ordering also covers the optional diagnostic neighbor_ids list (present-slot count and the stable-ID tie order); metric_status_honesty and metric_shape apply to comparison.metrics and mirror the acceptance_metric allOf rules in ../common.schema.json that this slice's JSON Schema subset does not evaluate.

path.description: What the expectation applies to, e.g. records.0; 'records' applies to the whole sequence; 'comparison' or 'comparison.metrics' applies to the metric list and 'comparison.metrics.N' to one metric.

statement.description: Human-readable restatement of the specified behavior being checked.
